title: Verbi Pronominali
subtitle: Farsi, andarsene, cavarsela — idiomatic verbs built from pronoun combinations.
objectives: Recognize pronominal verbs as fixed idiomatic units
Conjugate andarsene and cavarsela correctly across their pronoun set
Use common pronominal verbs naturally in context

content.intro: Pronominal verbs fuse a base verb with one or more pronouns into an idiomatic unit whose meaning often can't be guessed from the parts — a hallmark of fluent, native-sounding Italian.
content.explanation: Andarsene (to leave, to go away) combines the reflexive andarsi with ne, both of which move together through the conjugation. Cavarsela (to get by, to manage) combines cavarsi with la. These aren't literal reflexive/partitive meanings anymore — they're memorized as whole idiomatic verbs.

rules.heading: a) Common pronominal verbs
rules.body:
• farcela — to manage, to make it: Ce l'ho fatta! (I made it!)
  • cavarsela — to get by: Me la cavo bene in inglese. (I get by well in English.)
  • prendersela — to take offense/get upset: Non prendertela! (Don't take it personally!)
  • sentirsela — to feel up to something: Non me la sento di uscire stasera.

rules.heading: b) Passato prossimo of andarsene
rules.body: Takes essere, with the participle agreeing: Se n'è andato. (He left.) Se ne sono andate. (They [f.] left.)

examples.it: Me ne vado, ci vediamo domani.

examples.en: He/she got through the exam really well.

examples.it: Non prendertela, non era colpa tua.
examples.en: Don't take it personally, it wasn't your fault.

commonMistakes.why: Andarsene's pronouns (me/te/se/ce/ve/se + ne) precede the verb as a fixed unit — they can't be reordered or split.
The combined pronoun ce l' comes before the auxiliary, as one fixed sequence.

items.prompt: Sono stanco, ___ vado a dormire. (andarsene, io)
items.explanation: Io form of andarsene: me ne vado.
Ce l'ho fatta — I made it.

options: Don't take it (an object) with you.
Don't take offense / don't be upset about it.
Don't take it away from him.
items.explanation: Prendersela is an idiomatic pronominal verb meaning to take offense/get upset.

summary: Pronominal verbs (andarsene, cavarsela, farcela, prendersela) are idiomatic fixed units, not literal reflexive+pronoun combinations.
Their pronoun sequence moves together as a block through the conjugation.
Andarsene takes essere in the passato prossimo, with normal participle agreement.
